decisions.reason: The evening psychiatric day-patient program fits the firm's mental-health capabilities and can still reveal demand potential, so despite higher staffing intensity we would keep the option open for another year.
The carpentry workshop uses existing vocational and production know-how and may create both social and commercial value, so we would keep it while market acceptance is still being learned.
As a low-asset outpatient extension close to the core support model, sociotherapy is relatively inexpensive to continue and merits more time to prove demand.
Senior-living counseling is highly complementary to the eldercare business and likely low-cost to provide, making retention the better option.

The retail shop is a more peripheral and overhead-heavy commercialization step than the sheltered workshop itself, so with several other new options available we would be prepared to discontinue it if early traction is limited.
